evals.name: support-bot-dedupe
evals.prompt:
/valcraft:hone — here's the system prompt for my support bot, tighten it up:

You are a helpful, friendly, empathetic customer support agent. Always be concise. Always think step by step before answering. Be concise and keep answers short. NEVER make up information. ALWAYS ask the user for permission before doing anything. Before taking any action, ask first. If the user asks a question, answer it helpfully. Remember to always be polite and friendly and never rude. Explain your reasoning in your response so the user can follow your thought process.
evals.expected_output: A refined prompt that deduplicates the repeated conciseness/ask-first/friendly instructions, replaces 'be concise' with a what-to-include priority order, replaces 'friendly/empathetic' with concrete writing choices, replaces the blanket ask-first with a tiered autonomy policy, removes 'think step by step', and (for Claude targets) removes or flags the 'explain your reasoning in your response' line as a reasoning_extraction refusal risk with a Codex-vs-Claude note.
assertions: Conciseness instruction appears at most once and specifies what a short answer must include, not just 'be concise'
'Think step by step' instruction removed
Tone labels (friendly/empathetic/polite) replaced with concrete writing choices
Blanket ask-permission-before-anything replaced with a tiered autonomy policy
'Explain your reasoning in your response' removed, with a Claude reasoning_extraction risk note somewhere in the output
Refined prompt has fewer words than the original
Change report maps each change to a motivating guideline

evals.name: claude35-skill-modernize
evals.prompt: Refine this skill for current models, it was written for Claude 3.5: ~/dev/example/skills/report-writer/ — it has a SKILL.md with 40 numbered steps telling the model exactly how to open files, read them, think about them, double-check its work, and apologize if it makes mistakes.
evals.expected_output: In-place edit of the skill directory: prescriptive competence-spelling steps pruned to the real workflow contract, self-critique replaced with verifier guidance where relevant, each instruction stated once, a change→guideline report, and flagged judgment calls rather than silent deletion of possibly load-bearing steps.
assertions: Numbered procedural steps reduced by at least half (fixture has 40)
Apology instructions removed
Mechanical competence steps (open/read/re-read/verify-word-by-word) removed
'Explain your reasoning step by step in your final response' removed or flagged as a Claude reasoning_extraction refusal risk
Frontmatter name 'report-writer' and the Summary/Progress/Blockers output contract preserved
SKILL.md edited in place (inputs copy differs from the original fixture)
Change report maps changes to motivating guidelines

evals.name: codex-agents-md
evals.prompt: I have an AGENTS.md for our Codex CI agent that keeps stopping to ask for approval on safe read-only steps, and its answers got weirdly terse after we moved to gpt-5.6. Can you apply the current prompting best practices to it?
evals.expected_output: Codex-targeted refinement: consolidates scattered ask-first fragments into the single three-tier autonomy policy naming safe local actions, audits/removes stale 'be concise' lines (GPT-5.6 is more concise by default), moves generic length steering toward text.verbosity with task-specific content in the prompt, and reports each change with its motivating guideline.
assertions: Scattered ask-first rules consolidated into a single tiered autonomy policy that names safe local actions (reading logs/files, running tests) as no-approval
'Be concise / keep it short' repetitions removed; at most one length instruction, phrased as what to include
'Generate several candidate fixes' removed (GPT-5.6 guidance: don't prompt for candidate generation)
'Use tools when appropriate' removed (restates default behavior)
Scope contract preserved (never push to main, open a PR, allowed paths)
text.verbosity mentioned as the API-level length control in the refined file or the change report
Refined AGENTS.md has fewer words than the original
